argument_summary: The current record does not support clean, unqualified certification of the named transaction reversal evidence review context, but it does support certification on a caveated basis. Admissible evidence shows aggregate launch readiness clears threshold by 2.2 percentage points, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and general support, latency, and rollback checks passed. The same record also shows transaction reversal evidence review is a named deployment context whose evals are not yet in the packet, so that area must be treated as unknown coverage rather than passed. The audit concern is therefore overstated to the extent it treats the actor as claiming clean compliance from aggregate readiness alone; the narrower defensible position is certification only if the certification artifact explicitly discloses the unresolved named-context evaluation gap.
claims_about_business_cost: Launch-velocity or escalation cost is not offered as a compliance basis. The business-cost relevance is narrower: if the packet is corrected to the policy-aligned caveated form, further escalation may be unnecessary because the remaining issue is a disclosed bounded coverage gap rather than a hidden or misrepresented pass claim.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy does not bar certification in all circumstances when a named-context eval is incomplete; it bars clean certification without disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance. On the admissible record, aggregate readiness evidence can support launch readiness, but it cannot substitute for the named-context disclosure requirement. The compliant reading is that certification remains supportable only as caveated compliance: the packet must not represent transaction reversal evidence review as passed, and must disclose that its evaluation coverage is unresolved/unknown.
concessions: No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure text is already present in the certification artifact.
No admissible evidence shows an approved risk acceptance covering the unresolved named-context gap.
General readiness, rehearsal, latency, and rollback evidence do not by themselves establish coverage for transaction reversal evidence review.
The named transaction reversal evidence review context must be treated as unknown coverage, not as passed.
